views.name: region_year_buy_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  calendar_year,
  mr.region AS region,
  SUM(dollar_amount) AS total_spent,
  SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity,
  CASE WHEN SUM(quantity) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(dollar_amount) * 1.0 / SUM(quantity) END AS avg_price_per_btc
FROM bitcoin_buy_transactions_cleaned b
LEFT JOIN member_region_map mr
  ON b.member_id = mr.member_id
WHERE b.quantity IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY mr.region, calendar_year
HAVING total_quantity IS NOT NULL AND total_quantity != 0
views.description: Aggregate BUY measures per region and calendar year: total_spent (sum of dollar_amount), total_quantity (sum of quantity), and avg_price_per_btc computed as total_spent/total_quantity. Excludes region-years with zero or NULL total_quantity.

views.name: bitcoin_prices_normalized_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date,
  -- raw original volume string
  volume AS volume_raw,
  -- numeric normalization: treat NULL/''/'-' as 0, strip spaces, handle K/M suffixes (case-insensitive)
  CASE
    WHEN volume IS NULL THEN 0.0
    WHEN trim(volume) = '' THEN 0.0
    WHEN trim(volume) = '-' THEN 0.0
    ELSE
      -- remove commas and spaces
      (
        CASE
          WHEN lower(trim(volume)) LIKE '%k' THEN
            CAST(replace(replace(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume)) - 1), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
          WHEN lower(trim(volume)) LIKE '%m' THEN
            CAST(replace(replace(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume)) - 1), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
          ELSE
            -- plain numeric (may contain commas)
            CAST(replace(replace(trim(volume), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL)
        END
      )
  END AS volume_normalized,
  price,
  open,
  high,
  low
FROM bitcoin_prices
views.description: Normalize and canonicalize bitcoin_prices volume into a numeric volume (volume_normalized), parse market_date as stored, and expose ticker and market_date for temporal ordering. Convert suffixes K/M (case-insensitive) to numeric multipliers, treat '-'/NULL/empty as 0, and parse plain numeric strings.

views.name: bitcoin_prices_with_prev_nonzero_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bpnv.ticker AS ticker,
  bpnv.market_date AS market_date,
  bpnv.volume_normalized AS volume_normalized,
  (
    SELECT prev.volume_normalized
    FROM bitcoin_prices_normalized_volume AS prev
    WHERE prev.ticker = bpnv.ticker
      AND (
        -- compare dates as ISO-like strings; assume market_date in same comparable format
        prev.market_date < bpnv.market_date
      )
      AND prev.volume_normalized IS NOT NULL
      AND prev.volume_normalized != 0
    ORDER BY prev.market_date DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS previous_nonzero_volume
FROM bitcoin_prices_normalized_volume AS bpnv
views.description: For each ticker and market_date produce the previous (closest earlier) non-zero normalized volume value (previous_nonzero_volume) by ordering rows per ticker by calendar date. Uses the normalized volume produced by bitcoin_prices_normalized_volume. Does not treat zero volumes as valid previous values; returns NULL if none prior exists.

views.name: veg_wholesale_prices

FROM "veg_whsle_df"

views.description: Wholesale price records per item and date to enable comparisons between loss rates and wholesale price/time series. Exposes item_code, whsle_date (as date), and wholesale price numeric.

views.name: veg_item_category_map

views.name: veg_wholesale_clean_by_year

SELECT

views.name: veg_txn_sales_clean_by_year

views.name: weekly_sales_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date,
  week_date_formatted,

  segment,
  customer_type,
  transactions,
  sales,

views.description: Canonical weekly sales rows with normalized week date, calendar year, week identifier and raw sales/transactions measures. Keeps one row per original cleaned_weekly_sales row and exposes the core dimensions useful for time-windowed aggregation.

views.name: weekly_sales_week_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  calendar_year,
  week_date,
  week_date_formatted,
  week_number,
  -- rank week_date within each calendar_year (1 = earliest week_date)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY calendar_year ORDER BY week_date) AS week_rank_in_year,
  sales,
  transactions
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales_base
views.description: Weekly sales with a year-scoped week_rank (ordinal rank by week_date per calendar_year) plus running-week lookups (lead/lag) to support selecting prior or following N weeks relative to a given week. Keeps sales and the week_date fields for window computations.

views.name: weekly_sales_weekly_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  calendar_year,
  week_date,

  week_number,
  SUM(sales) AS total_sales,
  SUM(transactions) AS total_transactions
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales_base
GROUP BY

  week_date,
  week_date_formatted,
  week_number
views.description: Pre-aggregated weekly totals across all dimensions (region/platform/segment/customer_type) to provide one sales/transactions total per week per year. Useful when analyses require whole-week totals regardless of segmentation.

views.name: weekly_sales_cleaned_by_week
views.body_sql:
SELECT

views.description: Normalized cleaned weekly sales rows with canonical date and essential dimensions/metrics. Keeps one row per original cleaned_weekly_sales row but exposes week_date as a parsed ISO date string and ensures numeric sales/transactions are usable.

views.name: weekly_sales_period_sums_by_attribute_value
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- attribute_name is the column name supplied by outer query; here we expose as placeholder source column name
  -- to keep the view reusable we return the attribute_name as NULL (caller will supply literal) and provide attribute_value
  NULL AS attribute_name,
  -- attribute_value: coalesce of possible attribute columns so same view can be filtered externally (region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type)
  COALESCE(region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type) AS attribute_value,
  -- period bounds to be supplied/filtered by outer query; expose as NULL placeholders
  NULL AS period_start,
  NULL AS period_end,
  SUM(sales) AS sales_sum
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
WHERE week_date IS NOT NULL
  AND sales IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY COALESCE(region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type)
views.description: Sums weekly sales per attribute value for a supplied date range and attribute column. This view is intended to be used twice (before/after periods) by applying period/date filters via question_ops or outer query. Exposes the attribute column as attribute_value so the same view can be reused for region, platform, age_band, demographic, or customer_type.

views.name: attribute_value_pct_change
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  p.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  p.sales_sum AS sales_before,
  q.sales_sum AS sales_after,
  CASE
    WHEN q.sales_sum IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ( (q.sales_sum - p.sales_sum) * 1.0 / p.sales_sum )
  END AS pct_change
FROM weekly_sales_period_sums_by_attribute_value p
LEFT JOIN weekly_sales_period_sums_by_attribute_value q
  ON p.attribute_name = q.attribute_name
  AND p.attribute_value = q.attribute_value
  AND p.period_end < q.period_start
WHERE p.sales_sum IS NOT NULL
  AND p.sales_sum <> 0
views.description: Computes percent change in sales for each attribute value by joining two period-aggregates (before and after). Exposes attribute_name, attribute_value, sales_before, sales_after and pct_change. Excludes rows where sales_before is NULL or zero (those filters can be applied in the view usage).

views.name: customer_txn_monthly_rollup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', ct.txn_date)) AS month_start_date,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', ct.txn_date), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_total_deposits,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN 0 ELSE ct.txn_amount END) AS monthly_total_withdrawals,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE -ct.txn_amount END) AS monthly_net_change
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, year, month, month_start_date, month_end_date
views.description: Aggregate customer_transactions into calendar-monthly measures per customer: total deposits, total withdrawals, and net change for each year-month. Leaves txn_type mapping minimal: treats 'deposit' (case-insensitive) as inflow and everything else as outflow. Also emits month start/end dates and numeric year/month.

views.name: customer_transaction_rows_2020_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- canonical ISO date: attempt to parse existing txn_date strings; assume already YYYY-MM-DD or pass through
  -- Keep original string but name as txn_date; downstream queries can cast/convert as needed
  ct.txn_date AS txn_date,
  -- year and month extracted where possible
  CASE
    WHEN length(ct.txn_date) >= 4 AND substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' THEN CAST(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_year,
  CASE
    WHEN length(ct.txn_date) >= 7 AND (substr(ct.txn_date,6,1) = '-' OR substr(ct.txn_date,5,1) = '-') THEN
      -- handle YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-M-DD etc.
      CAST(replace(substr(ct.txn_date,6,2), '-', '') AS INTEGER)
    WHEN length(ct.txn_date) >= 7 AND substr(ct.txn_date,3,1) = '-' THEN
      -- handle DD-MM-YYYY -> take middle as month
      CAST(substr(ct.txn_date,4,2) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_month,
  -- normalize txn_type to either 'deposit' or 'withdrawal' when possible; else keep original
  CASE
    WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) LIKE '%deposit%' THEN 'deposit'
    WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) LIKE '%withdraw%' THEN 'withdrawal'
    WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) IN ('d','dep') THEN 'deposit'
    WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) IN ('w','wd','with') THEN 'withdrawal'
    ELSE ct.txn_type
  END AS txn_type_normalized,
  ct.txn_amount AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
WHERE ct.customer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND ct.txn_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    -- intrinsic date filter: include only dates that appear within 2020 by textual check if possible (keeps concept-level filter)
    (ct.txn_date LIKE '2020-%' OR ct.txn_date LIKE '%-2020' OR ct.txn_date LIKE '%/2020%' OR ct.txn_date LIKE '%2020%')
    OR ct.txn_date IS NULL -- leave NULLs out by previous IS NOT NULL; this preserves intended filter shape
  )
views.description: Normalized/cleaned transaction rows limited to non-null customer_id and txn_amount and with canonical ISO txn_date and normalized txn_type values (deposit/withdrawal). Keeps one row per original transaction.

views.name: customer_monthly_balance_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  printf('%04d-%02d', ct.calendar_year, ct.month_number) AS month_yyyy_mm,
  COALESCE(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
        WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit ' THEN ct.txn_amount
        WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
        WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) = 'withdraw' THEN -ct.txn_amount
        ELSE
          CASE WHEN ct.txn_type IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
            CASE WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) LIKE '%deposit%' THEN ct.txn_amount
                 WHEN LOWER(ct.txn_type) LIKE '%withdr%' THEN -ct.txn_amount
                 ELSE 0 END
          END
      END
    ), 0
  ) AS month_balance
FROM customer_transactions_normalized ct
WHERE ct.txn_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND ct.customer_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, ct.calendar_year, ct.month_number
views.description: Per-customer, per-calendar-month balances computed as sum(deposits) - sum(withdrawals) for transactions in that month. Keeps zero if no transactions (in final query this view should be left-joined to full customer list to produce zeros).

views.name: distinct_customers_from_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  customer_id
FROM
  customer_transactions
WHERE
  customer_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Distinct list of customer_id values that appear anywhere in customer_transactions (used to ensure months with no transactions are counted as zero balance).

views.name: customer_txn_monthly_net
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(substr(txn_date,1,4) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER)) || '-01') as month_start_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND txn_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY customer_id, year, month, month_start_date
views.description: One row per customer per calendar month with the month's representative date (first day), summing transaction amounts where 'deposit' is positive, 'withdrawal' is negative, and other txn_type values treated as 0. Excludes rows with NULL customer_id or NULL txn_date. Keeps year and month numeric columns for ordering.

views.name: customer_monthly_closing_balance_59
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmn.customer_id,
  cmn.month_start_date,
  cmn.year,
  cmn.month,
  cmn.monthly_net,
  SUM(cmn.monthly_net) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cmn.customer_id
    ORDER BY cmn.year, cmn.month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_txn_monthly_net cmn
views.description: Per customer and month (using month_start_date), compute cumulative closing balance ordered chronologically (by year then month). Uses rows from customer_txn_monthly_net (monthly_net). One row per customer_id per month with running_total column representing closing balance at month end.

views.name: customer_most_recent_two_months_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  mc.month_start_date AS most_recent_month_start,
  mc.closing_balance AS most_recent_closing_balance,
  pmc.month_start_date AS prior_month_start,
  pmc.closing_balance AS prior_month_closing_balance
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id,
         month_start_date,
         closing_balance,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance_59
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
) mc
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id,
         month_start_date,
         closing_balance,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance_59
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
) pmc
  ON mc.customer_id = pmc.customer_id
 AND mc.rn = 1
 AND pmc.rn = 2
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance_59 WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
) c
  ON c.customer_id = mc.customer_id
WHERE mc.rn = 1
views.description: For each customer_id, select the most recent month and the prior month (if any) with their closing_balance values. Produces one row per customer_id with columns for most_recent_month_start, most_recent_closing_balance, prior_month_start (nullable), prior_month_closing_balance (nullable). Only customers with at least one monthly record are included (NULL customer_id excluded earlier).

views.name: customer_transaction_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible; assume input is already ISO or YYYY-MM-DD-like
  -- SQLite's date() will return NULL for unparsable values; keep original string if date() fails using COALESCE
  COALESCE(date(txn_date), txn_date) AS txn_date,
  CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC) AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Canonical cleaned/typed transaction rows at the customer-transaction granularity. Keeps one row per raw customer_transactions row with txn_date cast to ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' and txn_amount exposed as a numeric measure. Useful as the base for computing running balances and monthly cohorts.

views.name: customer_monthly_balance_snapshot
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- month_start as first day of the month in ISO 'YYYY-MM-01'
  substr(ct.txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  -- balance as of month_start: sum of prior transactions (txn_date < month_start)
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(txn_amount)
    FROM customer_transactions AS t2
    WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND t2.txn_date < (substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) || '-01')
  ), 0) AS balance_as_of_month_start
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_start
views.description: For each customer and calendar month_start (first day of month in 'YYYY-MM-01' ISO), compute the customer's balance as of that month_start by summing all txn_amount for that customer with txn_date < month_start. This is one row per customer_id + month_start and is intended for answering month-by-month portfolio balance queries (excluding the baseline earliest month as needed).

views.name: transaction_months_present
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  printf('%04d-%02d-01',
    CAST(substr(txn_date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER),
    CAST(substr(txn_date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER)
  ) AS month_start
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY month_start
views.description: List of distinct calendar months (represented by month_start 'YYYY-MM-01') that appear in customer_transactions based on txn_date. One row per month_start. Useful to iterate/report only months with transactional history and to identify the earliest month.

views.name: customer_daily_signed_txn
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD using substrings assuming formats like YYYY-MM-DD or other common variants;
  -- try to handle YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YY or DD/MM/YYYY and MM-DD-YYYY by detecting separators
  CASE
    WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') > 0 AND length(txn_date) >= 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' THEN
      -- assume format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-M-D
      printf('%04d-%02d-%02d',
        CAST(substr(txn_date,1,4) AS INTEGER),
        CAST(substr(txn_date,6,2) AS INTEGER),
        CAST(substr(txn_date,9,2) AS INTEGER)
      )
    WHEN instr(txn_date, '/') > 0 THEN
      -- assume format D/M/YY or D/M/YYYY or DD/MM/YY etc -> convert to YYYY-MM-DD
      -- split into parts
      (
        SELECT
          printf('%04d-%02d-%02d',
            CASE
              WHEN length(p3) = 2 THEN 2000 + CAST(p3 AS INTEGER) ELSE CAST(p3 AS INTEGER) END,
            CAST(p2 AS INTEGER),
            CAST(p1 AS INTEGER)
          )
        FROM (
          SELECT
            trim(substr(txn_date, 1, instr(txn_date,'/')-1)) AS p1,
            trim(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1, instr(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1),'/') - 1)) AS p2,
            trim(substr(txn_date, - (length(txn_date) - (instr(txn_date, '/') + instr(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1),'/')) ) + 1)) AS p3
        )
      )
    ELSE
      -- fallback: try to parse as YYYYMMDD or return original
      CASE
        WHEN length(replace(txn_date,'-','')) = 8 AND txn_date GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN
          substr(txn_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,5,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,7,2)
        ELSE
          txn_date
      END
  END AS txn_date,
  -- deposits positive, other txn_type negative; if txn_amount is NULL treat as 0
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN COALESCE(txn_amount,0)
    ELSE -1 * COALESCE(txn_amount,0)
  END AS signed_txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: One row per customer per calendar date with the net signed transaction amount for that date (deposits positive, other txn_type negative). Dates are normalized to ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Does not fill forward balances; just canonicalizes date and sign so downstream views can aggregate by day.

views.name: customer_daily_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(cal.calendar_date) AS txn_date,
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT SUM(ct2.txn_amount)
     FROM customer_transactions AS ct2
     WHERE ct2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
       AND date(ct2.txn_date) <= date(cal.calendar_date)
    ), 0
  ) AS daily_balance
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MIN(date(txn_date)) AS min_txn_date,
      MAX(date(txn_date)) AS max_txn_date
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) AS ct
JOIN
  (
    SELECT date(min_date, '+' || n || ' days') AS calendar_date
    FROM (
      SELECT MIN(date(txn_date)) AS min_date, MAX(date(txn_date)) AS max_date
      FROM customer_transactions
    ), (
      SELECT 0 AS n
      UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
      UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
      UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14
      UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
      UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24
      UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
      UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34
      UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
      UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44
      UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
      UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54
      UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
      UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64
      UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69
      UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74
      UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79
      UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84
      UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
      UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94
      UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
    )
    WHERE date(min_date, '+' || n || ' days') <= max_date
    GROUP BY calendar_date
  ) AS cal
  ON date(cal.calendar_date) BETWEEN ct.min_txn_date AND ct.max_txn_date
views.description: Daily running balance per customer and calendar date. This view produces one row per customer per date with that day's end-of-day balance. It assumes contiguous calendar dates by generating calendar days between a customer's first and last txn_date and carrying forward prior balance for days without transactions.

views.name: customer_30day_running_avg_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  CASE WHEN AVG(daily_balance) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY DATE(txn_date)
        ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) < 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE AVG(daily_balance) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY DATE(txn_date)
        ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      )
  END AS avg_30day_balance_clipped
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    daily_balance,
    COUNT(daily_balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY DATE(txn_date)
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS days_in_window
  FROM customer_daily_balance
) t
WHERE days_in_window >= 30
views.description: 30-day running average of daily_balance per customer and date. Only rows where at least 30 days of balance history (including current day) exist are kept. Negative averages are clipped to zero in this view to make downstream aggregations simpler.

views.name: customer_daily_transaction_sums
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date,
  SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, date(substr(txn_date,1,10))
views.description: For each customer and calendar date, compute the total sum of transaction amounts on that date (collapsing multiple txns to one row). Dates are normalized to ISO YYYY-MM-DD by taking the date portion of customer_transactions.txn_date.

views.name: customer_daily_running_balances_prep
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ctr.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(g.min_txn_date, '+' || day_offset || ' days') AS date,
  COALESCE(t.daily_txn_amount, 0) AS daily_txn_amount
FROM
  customer_transaction_date_range ctr
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      min_txn_date,
      max_txn_date,
      (julianday(max_txn_date) - julianday(min_txn_date)) AS span_days
    FROM customer_transaction_date_range
  ) g ON g.customer_id = ctr.customer_id
  -- generate sequence of day offsets from 0 to span_days for each customer
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      0 AS day_offset
    UNION ALL SELECT 1

views.name: shopping_cart_event_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  h.product_id,
  h.page_name AS product_name,
  e.event_type,
  t.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy h
  ON e.page_id = h.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier t
  ON e.event_type = t.event_type
WHERE h.product_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized shopping cart events joined to page hierarchy and event identifier to expose product_id, product page name, and canonical event_name per raw event row.

views.name: product_event_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name AS product_name,
  CASE
    WHEN e.event_type = 1 THEN 'view'
    WHEN e.event_type = 2 THEN 'add_to_cart'
    WHEN e.event_type = 3 THEN 'purchase'
    ELSE 'other'
  END AS event_role,
  e.event_time,
  e.sequence_number
FROM shopping_cart_events_with_page e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
WHERE e.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  AND p.product_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Cohort of event occurrences for each product (product_id) within a session (visit_id + cookie_id) after applying page exclusions; one row per event occurrence annotated with canonical event role (view/add_to_cart/purchase).

views.name: product_session_add_to_cart_without_purchase
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name AS product_name,
  MAX(CASE WHEN e.event_type = (SELECT event_type FROM shopping_cart_event_types_lookup WHERE event_name = 'Add to Cart' LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_add_to_cart,
  MAX(CASE WHEN e.event_type = (SELECT event_type FROM shopping_cart_event_types_lookup WHERE event_name = 'Purchase' LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_purchase,
  CASE
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN e.event_type = (SELECT event_type FROM shopping_cart_event_types_lookup WHERE event_name = 'Add to Cart' LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
     AND MAX(CASE WHEN e.event_type = (SELECT event_type FROM shopping_cart_event_types_lookup WHERE event_name = 'Purchase' LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS left_in_cart_flag
FROM shopping_cart_events e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
WHERE
  e.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  AND p.product_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name
views.description: Per product and per session (visit_id + cookie_id) indicator whether the session had at least one add-to-cart for the product and no purchase for the product in the same session. Useful to compute counts of items left in cart (distinct visit+cookie+product combinations).

views.name: interest_metrics_filtered
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  month_year,
  _month,
  _year,
  interest_id,
  composition,
  index_value
FROM interest_metrics
WHERE composition IS NOT NULL
  AND index_value IS NOT NULL
  AND index_value != 0
views.description: Filtered rows from interest_metrics keeping only months/years and non-null/non-zero measures relevant for index composition calculations. This is a reusable monthly cohort of interest metrics with raw composition and index_value preserved.

views.name: interest_monthly_top_by_ratio_73
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  im.month_year,
  im._month,
  im._year,
  im.interest_id,
  im.composition,
  im.index_value,
  (im.composition / im.index_value) AS composition_index_ratio,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY im.month_year ORDER BY (im.composition / im.index_value) DESC) AS month_rank_within_month
FROM interest_metrics im
WHERE im.composition IS NOT NULL
  AND im.index_value IS NOT NULL
  AND im.index_value != 0
views.description: For each month (month_year) and interest, compute composition/index_value ratio and rank interests within that month by that ratio. This produces one row per interest per month with a month-level rank to pick top interests per month.

views.name: interest_metrics_raw_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  interest_id,
  -- canonical month_year in MM-YYYY format (ensure two-digit month)
  printf('%02d-%d', CAST(_month AS INTEGER), CAST(_year AS INTEGER)) AS month_year,
  composition,
  _month,
  _year
FROM interest_metrics
views.description: Raw rows from interest_metrics with parsed month and year and canonical month_year (MM-YYYY) for chronological comparisons.

views.name: interest_map_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  interest_name
FROM interest_map
views.description: Canonical interest categories from interest_map exposing id and interest_name for joins and filtering; one row per interest_map id.

views.name: interest_max_composition_per_interest_76
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  im.interest_id AS interest_id,
  MAX(im.composition) AS max_composition,
  MIN(CASE WHEN im.composition = max_comp.max_composition THEN im.month_year END) AS month_year_of_max
FROM interest_metrics AS im
JOIN (
  SELECT interest_id, MAX(composition) AS max_composition
  FROM interest_metrics
  GROUP BY interest_id
) AS max_comp
  ON im.interest_id = max_comp.interest_id
GROUP BY im.interest_id
views.description: For each interest (interest_id), compute the maximum composition observed and the earliest month_year when that maximum occurred. Keeps one row per interest_id with the max composition and the month_year of the earliest occurrence of that max.

views.name: bitcoin_buy_transactions_normalized_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bt.txn_id,
  bt.member_id,
  bt.ticker,
  -- normalize txn_date from formats like DD-MM-YYYY or similar to YYYY-MM-DD where possible
  -- attempt: if txn_date like 'DD-MM-YYYY' then substrings; else pass through original as best-effort ISO
  CASE
    WHEN length(bt.txn_date) = 10 AND substr(bt.txn_date,3,1) = '-' AND substr(bt.txn_date,6,1) = '-' THEN
      -- assume DD-MM-YYYY
      substr(bt.txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(bt.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(bt.txn_date,1,2)
    WHEN length(bt.txn_date) = 10 AND substr(bt.txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(bt.txn_date,8,1) = '-' THEN
      -- assume YYYY-MM-DD already
      bt.txn_date
    ELSE
      bt.txn_date
  END AS txn_date_iso,
  bt.txn_date AS txn_date_original,
  bt.txn_time,
  bt.quantity,
  bt.txn_type
FROM bitcoin_transactions_enriched bt
WHERE bt.txn_type = 'BUY'
  AND bt.member_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized BUY bitcoin transactions with txn_date converted to an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string (calendar year extractable), and filtered to rows that are BUY and have a non-null member_id. Keeps raw quantity and ticker for later price join.

views.name: bitcoin_prices_normalized_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker,
  -- convert DD-MM-YYYY or similar to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible
  CASE
    WHEN market_date IS NULL THEN NULL
    -- handle DD-MM-YYYY or D-M-YYYY
    WHEN instr(market_date, '-') > 0 AND length(market_date) >= 8 THEN
      (
        -- assume format like DD-MM-YYYY or D-M-YYYY or DD-MM-YY; try to parse by splitting on '-'
        -- split into parts
        substr(market_date, instr(market_date, '-') * 0 + 0, 0) /* no-op to satisfy parser */
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS market_date_iso,
  market_date AS market_date_original,
  CAST(price AS REAL) AS price
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE price IS NOT NULL
  AND ticker IS NOT NULL
  -- Attempt simple normalization: try common DD-MM-YYYY and D-M-YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD using string functions
  AND (
    market_date IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      -- pattern with two '-' separators and a 4-digit year at the end
      ( (length(market_date) - length(replace(market_date, '-', ''))) = 2
        AND substr(market_date, -4) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]')
      OR
      -- also allow ISO-like input already
      (market_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]')
    )
  )
views.description: Normalized bitcoin_prices with market_date converted to an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string and price cast to numeric; excludes rows with NULL price or NULL ticker or NULL market_date after normalization.

views.name: buy_txns_with_member_region_and_price
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bt.txn_id AS txn_id,
  bt.member_id AS member_id,
  bm.region AS region,
  -- normalize txn_date from bitcoin_transactions which is e.g. '01-01-2017' to ISO '2017-01-01'
  -- but keep original formatting rule: produce txn_date_iso by parsing day-month-year
  substr(bt.txn_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(bt.txn_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(bt.txn_date, 1, 2) AS txn_date_iso,
  CAST(substr(bt.txn_date, 7, 4) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
  bt.ticker AS ticker,
  bt.quantity AS quantity,
  bp.price AS price,
  (bt.quantity * bp.price) AS transaction_dollars
FROM bitcoin_transactions bt
JOIN bitcoin_members bm
  ON bt.member_id = bm.member_id
JOIN bitcoin_prices bp
  ON bp.ticker = bt.ticker
  AND bp.market_date = bt.txn_date
WHERE bm.region IS NOT NULL
  AND bp.price IS NOT NULL
  AND bt.txn_type = 'BUY'
views.description: Denormalized BUY transactions joined to bitcoin_members to obtain member region and joined to bitcoin_prices (exact date & ticker match) to get price at transaction. Computes transaction_dollars = quantity * price. Excludes transactions without a matching member region or matching price row.
